passages.text: Then the LORD sent Nathan to David, and when he arrived, he said, “There were two men in a certain city, one rich and the other poor.
passages.sermon:
The LORD sent Nathan to David.
Nathan went to David.
Nathan spoke to David.
Nathan said, “There were two men in one city.
One man was rich.
The other man was poor.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֧ח יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ נָתָ֖ן אֶל־ דָּוִ֑ד וַיָּבֹ֣א אֵלָ֗יו וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ שְׁנֵ֣י אֲנָשִׁ֗ים הָיוּ֙ בְּעִ֣יר אֶחָ֔ת אֶחָ֥ד עָשִׁ֖יר וְאֶחָ֥ד רָֽאשׁ׃

passages.text: The rich man had a great number of sheep and cattle, but the poor man had nothing except one small ewe lamb that he had bought. He raised it, and it grew up with him and his children. It shared his food and drank from his cup; it slept in his arms and was like a daughter to him.
passages.sermon:
There were two men in a city.
One man was rich.
The rich man owned many sheep.
He also owned many cattle.
The other man was poor.
The poor man owned nothing.
He had only one small female lamb.
He bought this lamb.
He cared for the lamb.
The lamb grew up with him.
The lamb also grew up with his children.
The lamb ate from his food.
The lamb drank from his cup.
The lamb slept in his arms.
The lamb was like a daughter to him.
passages.original: לְעָשִׁ֗יר הָיָ֛ה צֹ֥אן וּבָקָ֖ר הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃ וְלָרָ֣שׁ אֵֽין־ כֹּ֗ל כִּי֩ אִם־ כִּבְשָׂ֨ה אַחַ֤ת קְטַנָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָנָ֔ה וַיְחַיֶּ֕הָ וַתִּגְדַּ֥ל עִמּ֛וֹ וְעִם־ בָּנָ֖יו יַחְדָּ֑ו מִפִּתּ֨וֹ תֹאכַ֜ל וּמִכֹּס֤וֹ תִשְׁתֶּה֙ וּבְחֵיק֣וֹ תִשְׁכָּ֔ב וַתְּהִי־ ל֖וֹ כְּבַֽת׃

passages.text: Now a traveler came to the rich man, who refrained from taking one of his own sheep or cattle to prepare for the traveler who had come to him. Instead, he took the poor man’s lamb and prepared it for his guest.”
passages.sermon:
A traveler came to visit the rich man.
The rich man had many sheep and cattle.
The rich man did not want to take one of his own animals.
He did not want to use his own sheep or cattle for the traveler.
The rich man took the poor man’s only lamb.
He prepared the poor man’s lamb for his guest.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣בֹא הֵלֶךְ֮ לְאִ֣ישׁ הֶֽעָשִׁיר֒ וַיַּחְמֹ֗ל לָקַ֤חַת מִצֹּאנוֹ֙ וּמִבְּקָר֔וֹ לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת לָאֹרֵ֖חַ הַבָּא־ ל֑וֹ וַיִּקַּ֗ח אֶת־ כִּבְשַׂת֙ הָאִ֣ישׁ הָרָ֔אשׁ וַֽיַּעֲשֶׂ֔הָ לָאִ֖ישׁ הַבָּ֥א אֵלָֽיו׃

passages.text: David burned with anger against the man and said to Nathan: “As surely as the LORD lives, the man who did this deserves to die!
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David heard about the rich man’s actions.
David became very angry at the man.
David spoke to Nathan the prophet.
David said, “As surely as the LORD lives, the man who did this deserves to die.”
passages.original: וַיִּֽחַר־ אַ֥ף דָּוִ֛ד בָּאִ֖ישׁ מְאֹ֑ד וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ נָתָ֔ן חַי־ יְהוָ֕ה כִּ֣י בֶן־ מָ֔וֶת הָאִ֖ישׁ הָעֹשֶׂ֥ה זֹֽאת׃

passages.text: Because he has done this thing and has shown no pity, he must pay for the lamb four times over.”
passages.sermon:
The rich man took the poor man's lamb.
He did not show pity.
He must pay for the lamb.
He must pay four times over.
He must do this because he did this thing.
He must do this because he showed no mercy.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ הַכִּבְשָׂ֖ה יְשַׁלֵּ֣ם אַרְבַּעְתָּ֑יִם עֵ֗קֶב אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשָׂה֙ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וְעַ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־ חָמָֽל׃

passages.text: Then Nathan said to David, “You are that man! This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you from the hand of Saul.
passages.sermon:
Nathan spoke to David.
Nathan said, “You are that man.”
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD said this to David.
The LORD said, “I anointed you as king over Israel.”
The LORD said, “I rescued you from Saul.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר נָתָ֛ן אֶל־ דָּוִ֖ד אַתָּ֣ה הָאִ֑ישׁ כֹּה־ אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָנֹכִ֞י מְשַׁחְתִּ֤יךָֽ לְמֶ֙לֶךְ֙ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָנֹכִ֥י הִצַּלְתִּ֖יךָ מִיַּ֥ד שָׁאֽוּל׃

passages.text: I gave your master’s house to you and your master’s wives into your arms. I gave you the house of Israel and Judah, and if that was not enough, I would have given you even more.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD spoke to David.
The LORD made David king over Israel.
The LORD gave David Saul’s house.
The LORD gave David Saul’s wives.
The LORD placed Saul’s wives in David’s care.
The LORD gave David the house of Israel.
The LORD gave David the house of Judah.
If this had been too little, the LORD would have given David even more.
passages.original: וָאֶתְּנָ֨ה לְךָ֜ אֶת־ בֵּ֣ית אֲדֹנֶ֗יךָ וְאֶת־ נְשֵׁ֤י אֲדֹנֶ֙יךָ֙ בְּחֵיקֶ֔ךָ וָאֶתְּנָ֣ה לְךָ֔ אֶת־ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וִֽיהוּדָ֑ה וְאִ֨ם־ מְעָ֔ט וְאֹסִ֥פָה לְּךָ֖ כָּהֵ֥נָּה וְכָהֵֽנָּה׃

passages.text: Why then have you despised the command of the LORD by doing evil in His sight? You put Uriah the Hittite to the sword and took his wife as your own, for you have slain him with the sword of the Ammonites.
passages.sermon:
David was king of Israel.
Nathan spoke to David.
Nathan said, “You have despised the command of the LORD.
You did evil in the sight of God.
You struck down Uriah the Hittite with a sword.
You took Uriah’s wife to be your own wife.
You killed Uriah with the sword of the Ammonites.”
passages.original: מַדּ֜וּעַ בָּזִ֣יתָ׀ אֶת־ דְּבַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת הָרַע֮ בְּעֵינוֹ אֵ֣ת אוּרִיָּ֤ה הַֽחִתִּי֙ הִכִּ֣יתָ בַחֶ֔רֶב וְאֶ֨ת־ אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ לָקַ֥חְתָּ לְּךָ֖ לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וְאֹת֣וֹ הָרַ֔גְתָּ בְּחֶ֖רֶב בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Now, therefore, the sword will never depart from your house, because you have despised Me and have taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your own.’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to David through Nathan the prophet.
God said David had sinned.
God said David took Uriah the Hittite’s wife for himself.
God said David despised Him.
God said, “The sword will never leave your house.”
God said this punishment would last forever.
God said this would happen because David despised Him and took Uriah’s wife.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה לֹא־ תָס֥וּר חֶ֛רֶב מִבֵּיתְךָ֖ עַד־ עוֹלָ֑ם עֵ֚קֶב כִּ֣י בְזִתָ֔נִי וַתִּקַּ֗ח אֶת־ אֵ֙שֶׁת֙ אוּרִיָּ֣ה הַחִתִּ֔י לִהְי֥וֹת לְךָ֖ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: ‘I will raise up adversity against you from your own house. Before your very eyes I will take your wives and give them to another, and he will lie with them in broad daylight.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking.
The LORD says this to David.
The LORD will bring trouble against David.
This trouble will come from David’s own family.
The LORD will take David’s wives.
The LORD will do this while David watches.
The LORD will give David’s wives to another man.
This man will sleep with David’s wives.
He will do this in the open.
He will do this in broad daylight.
passages.original: כֹּ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִנְנִי֩ מֵקִ֨ים עָלֶ֤יךָ רָעָה֙ מִבֵּיתֶ֔ךָ וְלָקַחְתִּ֤י אֶת־ נָשֶׁ֙יךָ֙ לְעֵינֶ֔יךָ וְנָתַתִּ֖י לְרֵעֶ֑יךָ וְשָׁכַב֙ עִם־ נָשֶׁ֔יךָ לְעֵינֵ֖י הַשֶּׁ֥מֶשׁ הַזֹּֽאת׃

passages.text: You have acted in secret, but I will do this thing in broad daylight before all Israel.’ ”
passages.sermon:
David was king of Israel.
David sinned by taking the wife of Uriah the Hittite.
God spoke to David through Nathan the prophet.
God said, “You acted in secret.
You tried to hide your sin.
I will act openly.
I will do this thing in front of all Israel.
I will do it in broad daylight.”
passages.original: כִּ֥י אַתָּ֖ה עָשִׂ֣יתָ בַסָּ֑תֶר וַאֲנִ֗י אֶעֱשֶׂה֙ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה נֶ֥גֶד כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְנֶ֥גֶד הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃ס

passages.text: Then David said to Nathan, “I have sinned against the LORD.” “The LORD has taken away your sin,” Nathan replied. “You will not die.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke to Nathan the prophet.
David said, “I have sinned against the LORD.”
Nathan replied to David.
Nathan said, “The LORD has taken away your sin.”
Nathan said, “You will not die.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־ נָתָ֔ן חָטָ֖אתִי לַֽיהוָ֑הס וַיֹּ֨אמֶר נָתָ֜ן אֶל־ דָּוִ֗ד גַּם־ יְהוָ֛ה הֶעֱבִ֥יר חַטָּאתְךָ֖ לֹ֥א תָמֽוּת׃

passages.text: Nevertheless, because by this deed you have shown utter contempt for the word of the LORD, the son born to you will surely die.”
passages.sermon:
David is the king of Israel.
David sinned against the LORD.
Nathan is a prophet of God.
Nathan spoke to David.
Nathan said, “You have done this evil thing.
By this deed, you have shown utter contempt for the LORD.
You have given the LORD’s enemies a reason to speak against Him.
Because of this, the son born to you will surely die.”
passages.original: אֶ֗פֶס כִּֽי־ נִאֵ֤ץ נִאַ֙צְתָּ֙ אֶת־ אֹיְבֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה בַּדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה גַּ֗ם הַבֵּ֛ן הַיִּלּ֥וֹד לְךָ֖ מ֥וֹת יָמֽוּת׃

passages.text: After Nathan had gone home, the LORD struck the child that Uriah’s wife had borne to David, and he became ill.
passages.sermon:
Nathan was a prophet.
Nathan spoke to David.
Nathan went to his house.
David was king of Israel.
David had taken Uriah’s wife.
Uriah’s wife gave birth to a child for David.
The LORD acted.
The LORD struck the child.
The child became very sick.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ נָתָ֖ן אֶל־ בֵּית֑וֹ וַיִּגֹּ֣ף יְהוָ֗ה אֶת־ הַיֶּ֜לֶד אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָלְדָ֧ה אֵֽשֶׁת־ אוּרִיָּ֛ה לְדָוִ֖ד וַיֵּאָנַֽשׁ׃

passages.text: David pleaded with God for the boy. He fasted and went into his house and spent the night lying in sackcloth on the ground.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David’s son became very sick.
David pleaded with God to save his son.
David fasted.
He did not eat any food.
David went into his house.
He spent the night there.
He lay on the ground all night.
passages.original: וַיְבַקֵּ֥שׁ דָּוִ֛ד אֶת־ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּעַ֣ד הַנָּ֑עַר וַיָּ֤צָם דָּוִד֙ צ֔וֹם וּבָ֥א וְלָ֖ן וְשָׁכַ֥ב אָֽרְצָה׃

passages.text: The elders of his household stood beside him to help him up from the ground, but he was unwilling and would not eat anything with them.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David’s child was very sick.
David lay on the ground all night.
The elders of David’s household came to him.
They stood beside David.
They tried to help David get up from the ground.
David refused to get up.
David would not eat with them.
passages.original: וַיָּקֻ֜מוּ זִקְנֵ֤י בֵיתוֹ֙ עָלָ֔יו לַהֲקִימ֖וֹ מִן־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וְלֹ֣א אָבָ֔ה וְלֹֽא־ בָרָ֥א אִתָּ֖ם לָֽחֶם׃

passages.text: On the seventh day the child died. But David’s servants were afraid to tell him that the child was dead, for they said, “Look, while the child was alive, we spoke to him, and he would not listen to us. So how can we tell him the child is dead? He may even harm himself.”
passages.sermon:
On the seventh day, the child died.
David was the father of the child.
David’s servants saw that the child had died.
The servants were afraid to tell David that the child was dead.
The servants said, “While the child was alive, we spoke to David.”
David did not listen to the servants.
The servants said, “How can we tell David that the child is dead?”
The servants feared David might harm himself.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֛י בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י וַיָּ֣מָת הַיָּ֑לֶד וַיִּֽרְאוּ֩ עַבְדֵ֨י דָוִ֜ד לְהַגִּ֥יד ל֣וֹ׀ כִּי־ מֵ֣ת הַיֶּ֗לֶד כִּ֤י אָֽמְרוּ֙ הִנֵּה֩ בִהְי֨וֹת הַיֶּ֜לֶד חַ֗י דִּבַּ֤רְנוּ אֵלָיו֙ וְלֹא־ שָׁמַ֣ע בְּקוֹלֵ֔נוּ וְאֵ֨יךְ נֹאמַ֥ר אֵלָ֛יו מֵ֥ת הַיֶּ֖לֶד וְעָשָׂ֥ה רָעָֽה׃

passages.text: When David saw that his servants were whispering to one another, he perceived that the child was dead. So he asked his servants, “Is the child dead?” “He is dead,” they replied.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David saw his servants whispering to each other.
David understood that the child had died.
David spoke to his servants.
David asked, “Is the child dead?”
The servants answered David.
They said, “He is dead.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֣רְא דָּוִ֗ד כִּ֤י עֲבָדָיו֙ מִֽתְלַחֲשִׁ֔ים וַיָּ֥בֶן דָּוִ֖ד כִּ֣י מֵ֣ת הַיָּ֑לֶד וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֧ד אֶל־ עֲבָדָ֛יו הֲמֵ֥ת הַיֶּ֖לֶד וַיֹּ֥אמְרוּ מֵֽת׃

passages.text: Then David got up from the ground, washed and anointed himself, changed his clothes, and went into the house of the LORD and worshiped. Then he went to his own house, and at his request they set food before him, and he ate.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David had been lying on the ground.
David got up from the ground.
David washed himself.
David anointed himself with oil.
David changed his clothes.
David went into the house of the LORD.
David worshiped the LORD there.
David went to his own house.
David asked for food.
They set food before David.
David ate the food.
passages.original: וַיָּקָם֩ דָּוִ֨ד מֵהָאָ֜רֶץ וַיִּרְחַ֣ץ וַיָּ֗סֶךְ וַיְחַלֵּף֙ שִׂמְלָתוֹ וַיָּבֹ֥א בֵית־ יְהוָ֖ה וַיִּשְׁתָּ֑חוּ וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל־ בֵּית֔וֹ וַיִּשְׁאַ֕ל וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ ל֛וֹ לֶ֖חֶם וַיֹּאכַֽל׃

passages.text: “What is this you have done?” his servants asked. “While the child was alive, you fasted and wept, but when he died, you got up and ate.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David’s child had been very sick.
David’s servants spoke to him.
They asked David a question.
They said, “What is this thing you have done?”
They said, “While the child was alive, you fasted.”
They said, “You also wept.”
They said, “But when the child died, you got up.”
They said, “You ate food.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ עֲבָדָיו֙ אֵלָ֔יו מָֽה־ הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑יתָה בַּעֲב֞וּר הַיֶּ֤לֶד חַי֙ צַ֣מְתָּ וַתֵּ֔בְךְּ וְכַֽאֲשֶׁר֙ מֵ֣ת הַיֶּ֔לֶד קַ֖מְתָּ וַתֹּ֥אכַל לָֽחֶם׃

passages.text: David answered, “While the child was alive, I fasted and wept, for I said, ‘Who knows? The LORD may be gracious to me and let him live.’
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke to his servants.
David said, "While the child was alive, I fasted."
David said, "I also wept while the child lived."
David explained his reason.
David said, "I thought, 'Who knows?'
David said, "The LORD may be gracious to me."
David said, "The LORD may let the child live."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בְּעוֹד֙ הַיֶּ֣לֶד חַ֔י צַ֖מְתִּי וָֽאֶבְכֶּ֑ה כִּ֤י אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ מִ֣י יוֹדֵ֔עַ יְחָנַּנִי יְהוָ֖ה וְחַ֥י הַיָּֽלֶד׃

passages.text: But now that he is dead, why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I will go to him, but he will not return to me.”
passages.sermon:
David spoke about his dead child.
The child is now dead.
I cannot change this.
Why should I fast now?
I cannot bring him back to life.
One day, I will go to him.
He will not return to me.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֣ה׀ מֵ֗ת לָ֤מָּה זֶּה֙ אֲנִ֣י צָ֔ם הַאוּכַ֥ל לַהֲשִׁיב֖וֹ ע֑וֹד אֲנִי֙ הֹלֵ֣ךְ אֵלָ֔יו וְה֖וּא לֹֽא־ יָשׁ֥וּב אֵלָֽי׃

passages.text: Then David comforted his wife Bathsheba, and he went to her and lay with her. So she gave birth to a son, and they named him Solomon. Now the LORD loved the child and sent word through Nathan the prophet to name him Jedidiah because the LORD loved him.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Bathsheba was David’s wife.
David comforted Bathsheba.
David went to Bathsheba.
David lay with Bathsheba.
Bathsheba gave birth to a son.
David and Bathsheba named their son Solomon.
The LORD loved Solomon.
The LORD sent a message through Nathan the prophet.
The LORD told Nathan to name the boy Jedidiah.
The LORD chose the name Jedidiah because He loved the child.
passages.original: וַיְנַחֵ֣ם דָּוִ֗ד אֵ֚ת בַּת־ שֶׁ֣בַע אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֥א אֵלֶ֖יהָ וַיִּשְׁכַּ֣ב עִמָּ֑הּ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֗ן וַיִּקְרָא אֶת־ שְׁמוֹ֙ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַיהוָ֖ה אֲהֵבֽוֹ׃ וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח בְּיַד֙ נָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֔יא וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־ שְׁמ֖וֹ יְדִ֣ידְיָ֑הּ בַּעֲב֖וּר יְהוָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Meanwhile, Joab fought against Rabbah of the Ammonites and captured the royal fortress.
passages.sermon:
Joab was a commander in David’s army.
Joab fought against the city of Rabbah.
Rabbah belonged to the Ammonites.
Joab captured the royal fortress in Rabbah.
passages.original: וַיִּלָּ֣חֶם יוֹאָ֔ב בְּרַבַּ֖ת בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן וַיִּלְכֹּ֖ד אֶת־ עִ֥יר הַמְּלוּכָֽה׃

passages.text: Then Joab sent messengers to David to say, “I have fought against Rabbah and have captured the water supply of the city.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Joab sent messengers to King David.
Joab said, “I have fought against Rabbah.
I have captured the city’s water supply.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח יוֹאָ֛ב מַלְאָכִ֖ים אֶל־ דָּוִ֑ד וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ נִלְחַ֣מְתִּי בְרַבָּ֔ה גַּם־ לָכַ֖דְתִּי אֶת־ עִ֥יר הַמָּֽיִם׃

passages.text: Now, therefore, assemble the rest of the troops, lay siege to the city, and capture it. Otherwise I will capture the city, and it will be named after me.”
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Joab spoke to David.
Joab said, “Gather the rest of the soldiers.
Go to the city.
Set up camp against the city.
Take the city.
If you do not take the city, I will take it.
If I take the city, people will name the city after me.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה אֱסֹף֙ אֶת־ יֶ֣תֶר הָעָ֔ם וַחֲנֵ֥ה עַל־ הָעִ֖יר וְלָכְדָ֑הּ פֶּן־ אֶלְכֹּ֤ד אֲנִי֙ אֶת־ הָעִ֔יר וְנִקְרָ֥א שְׁמִ֖י עָלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: So David assembled all the troops and went to Rabbah; and he fought against it and captured it.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David gathered all the troops of Israel.
David went to the city of Rabbah.
David fought against the city of Rabbah.
David captured the city of Rabbah.
passages.original: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֥ף דָּוִ֛ד אֶת־ כָּל־ הָעָ֖ם וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ רַבָּ֑תָה וַיִּלָּ֥חֶם בָּ֖הּ וַֽיִּלְכְּדָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Then he took the crown from the head of their king. It weighed a talent of gold and was set with precious stones, and it was placed on David’s head. And David took a great amount of plunder from the city.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David captured the city of Rabbah.
David took the crown from the head of the Ammonite king.
The crown weighed a talent of gold.
The crown had a precious stone in it.
They placed the crown on David’s head.
David took much plunder from the city.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת־ עֲטֶֽרֶת־ מַלְכָּם֩ מֵעַ֨ל רֹאשׁ֜וֹ וּמִשְׁקָלָ֨הּ כִּכַּ֤ר זָהָב֙ וְאֶ֣בֶן יְקָרָ֔ה וַתְּהִ֖י עַל־ רֹ֣אשׁ דָּוִ֑ד וּשְׁלַ֥ל הָעִ֛יר הוֹצִ֖יא הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: David brought out the people who were there and put them to work with saws, iron picks, and axes, and he made them work at the brick kilns. He did the same to all the Ammonite cities. Then David and all his troops returned to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David captured the city of Rabbah.
David took the people who lived in the city.
David made these people work with saws.
David made them use iron picks.
David made them use iron axes.
David made them work at the brick kilns.
David did the same thing in every city of the Ammonites.
David and all his soldiers returned to Jerusalem.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ הָעָ֨ם אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֜הּ הוֹצִ֗יא וַיָּ֣שֶׂם בַּ֠מְּגֵרָה וּבַחֲרִצֵ֨י הַבַּרְזֶ֜ל וּֽבְמַגְזְרֹ֣ת הַבַּרְזֶ֗ל וְהֶעֱבִ֤יר אוֹתָם֙ בַּמַּלְכֶּן וְכֵ֣ן יַעֲשֶׂ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל עָרֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־ עַמּ֑וֹן וַיָּ֧שָׁב דָּוִ֛ד וְכָל־ הָעָ֖ם יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃פ
